findings.description: Multiline Python signatures incorrectly terminate the function scope. For a conventional signature such as `def f(\n    argument,\n):`, the closing `):` has the definition's indentation, so this condition returns before the function body.
findings.failure_mode: Every body line receives no function scope. A citation and planted defect in the same function, but more than three lines apart, are consequently graded as a miss, producing incorrect recall scores and potentially failing an otherwise passing evaluation.
findings.suggested_fix: Identify the end of the complete Python signature before checking body dedentation, preferably using Python tokenization or AST function spans.

findings.description: When `yq eval ... | tag` fails (no .loa.config.yaml present, unparsable YAML, yq missing), the fallback echoes the literal `unreadable`, which is neither `!!null` nor empty. The function then sets CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET=true, logs a WARN with the odd text `budget_scale='(a unreadable, not a string)' is not fixed or diff`, and the envelope gains budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max and `reason: budget`. Every other config read in load_adversarial_config degrades silently to its default on a yq failure; this one changes the envelope shape, contradicting the documented contract that an absent key leaves the envelope byte-for-byte unchanged.
findings.failure_mode: Runs in a checkout with no .loa.config.yaml (or a temporarily unreadable one) emit a spurious WARN on every invocation and produce a different envelope shape than the same config did before this change, which can break consumers or fixtures that compare the metadata object exactly.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a yq failure as absent: `_bt=$(yq ... 2>/dev/null || echo '!!null')`, or test `[[ -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]` before reading and return 0 otherwise, so CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET stays false unless a key is genuinely written.

findings.description: `[[ "$_budget_meta" == "{}" ]] || result=$(echo "$result" | jq --argjson bm "$_budget_meta" ...)` assumes `_budget_meta` was initialised at the budget gate ~300 lines earlier. If any path reaches the envelope assembly without passing through the gate (the variable is `local` and only assigned there), `$_budget_meta` is empty, the test is false, `jq --argjson bm ""` fails, and under `set -e` the failed assignment either aborts main or clobbers `result` with an empty string after all voices have already been paid for.
findings.failure_mode: A control-flow path that skips the pre-dispatch estimate (e.g. a future flag or an early branch) turns a completed dissent run into an aborted one with an empty envelope.
findings.suggested_fix: Default the guard: `[[ "${_budget_meta:-\{\}}" == "{}" ]] || ...`, or initialise `local _budget_meta="{}"` at the top of main alongside the other locals.

findings.description: Two end-of-definition heuristics misfire on bash. (1) CLOSE_ONE (`\{.*\}\s*(?:#.*)?$`) plus `"{" in header` treats any header whose trailing comment ends in `}` — e.g. `f() {  # writes ${OUT}` — as a one-line function, so the whole body gets no scope and clause (ii) can never credit a defect inside it. (2) The `}` match compares raw `len(t)-len(t.lstrip())` to `lv`, but `lv` was computed with `expandtabs(8)` in headers(); a tab-indented nested function never finds its closing brace and runs to the next header.
findings.failure_mode: Grader under-credits: a review that cites the right function but not within ±3 of the site is scored as a miss for any function whose header comment contains `}` or whose body is tab-indented, skewing recall and the credits_function_only diagnostic.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip the trailing comment before the one-line test (e.g. match `\{[^#]*\}\s*(?:#.*)?$` against the header with `#...` removed, or require the `}` to be followed only by `;`/whitespace), and compute the `}` indentation with `len(t.expandtabs(8)) - len(t.expandtabs(8).lstrip())` to match headers().

findings.description: When EVAL_HEAD_DIR is unset and the fixture has no `<manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head`, the grader falls back to `$workspace/pr/head`, which is the agent-writable sandbox copy. The 1.3.0 rule now reads that tree for citation validity (line counts) and for definition scopes. An agent that rewrites a file under pr/head so that the whole file becomes one ≤400-line function makes any single citation in that file count for every defect in it. The ablation-grade header in this same PR states the harness never reads the sandbox pr/ for grading, so the grader's own fallback is inconsistent with that invariant.
findings.failure_mode: In a standalone or misconfigured grader invocation, the same-scope credit can be gamed by sandbox edits, inflating recall relative to the pm3 baseline.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `$workspace/pr/head` fallback (require EVAL_HEAD_DIR or the fixture head), or when it is used, disable clause (ii) and the length-validity rule and record `head_dir_source: sandbox` in details so the row writer can flag it.

findings.cross_file_justification: main() now emits `reason: "budget"` in the budget_exceeded envelope metadata, and the same PR edits the metadata schema (additionalProperties: false) to add budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max but not `reason`.
findings.description: The schema is updated for the three budget_* keys but not for the new `reason` key written beside them, while `additionalProperties: false` remains on metadata. The documented contract therefore rejects the exact envelope this change produces under budget_scale set + budget exceeded.
findings.failure_mode: Any consumer or test that validates the envelope against adversarial-finding.schema.json fails on a budget_exceeded envelope from a config that sets budget_scale.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `reason` (enum: ["budget"], description tied to cycle-131 FR-4) to the metadata properties, or drop `reason` from the envelope and rely on `status: budget_exceeded`.
